title: Weak Goldbach Conjecture (Ternary Goldbach)
description: Formalizes the Weak Goldbach Conjecture (proved by Helfgott 2013): every odd integer >5 is a sum of three primes. Axiomatizes Vinogradov's circle method, Helfgott's proof, Schnirelmann density, Ramare's 6-prime bound, Tao's 5-prime bound, and Chen's theorem. Proves structural reductions: binary Goldbach implies ternary, Lévy's conjecture verified for small cases. 27 theorems, 9 axioms.

meta.assumptions: 9 axioms for deep analytic number theory results: vinogradov_ternary_goldbach (Vinogradov 1937: every sufficiently large odd number is sum of 3 primes), helfgott_weak_goldbach (Helfgott 2013: proved unconditionally for all odd n>5), circle_method_asymptotic (circle method asymptotic formula for ternary representations), schnirelmann_basis_theorem (every dense enough set is an additive basis), ramare_six_primes (Ramare 1995: every even n > 1 is sum of ≤ 6 primes), tao_five_primes (Tao 2012: every odd n > 1 is sum of ≤ 5 primes), chen_theorem (Chen 1973: every sufficiently large even n = p + P₂), binary_goldbach_verified (verified for n ≤ 4·10¹⁸), helfgott_explicit_bound (Helfgott's explicit bound).

overview.historicalContext: The Weak Goldbach Conjecture (also: Ternary Goldbach Conjecture) states every odd integer >5 is the sum of three primes. This was conjectured by Goldbach in 1742. Vinogradov (1937) proved it for all sufficiently large odd integers using the circle method (exponential sums). Helfgott (2013) completed the proof unconditionally for all odd n > 5, making this one of the most recently resolved classical open problems. The stronger Binary Goldbach Conjecture (every even n > 2 = p+q) remains open.
overview.problemStatement: Prove: every odd integer n > 5 is the sum of three prime numbers. Develop the circle method infrastructure and axiomatize the key analytic results.
overview.text: The proof follows Vinogradov's circle method: write the number of ternary representations as an exponential sum over primes, split into major and minor arcs, and show the major arc contribution dominates. For small odd numbers, verify directly. Helfgott's 2013 proof gives an explicit bound making the verification finite + the Vinogradov asymptotic. The reduction binary → ternary is proved: if n is odd, then n = 2 + (n-2), and if n-2 is even with Goldbach representation p+q, then n = 2+p+q.
overview.proofStrategy: Axiomatize Helfgott's result. Prove structural reductions (binary → ternary). Define circle method infrastructure (exponential sums, representation count). Axiomatize intermediate results in the proof hierarchy (Vinogradov, Schnirelmann, Ramare, Tao, Chen). Verify small cases directly.
keyInsights: Circle method: split integration over residues into major arcs (near rationals p/q, small q) and minor arcs
Binary Goldbach implies ternary: every odd n = 2 + (n-2), use binary for even n-2
Schnirelmann density: if A has density > 0, A+A+...+A (k times) covers all sufficiently large integers
Chen's theorem (1973): every large even n = p + P₂ (prime + product of ≤2 primes) — just one step from binary Goldbach
prerequisites: Circle method: Hardy-Littlewood-Vinogradov exponential sum technique
Dirichlet series and L-functions for prime distribution

conclusion.summary: Weak Goldbach Conjecture formalized: statement, structural reductions, circle method infrastructure, Lévy verification for small cases. Helfgott 2013 proof axiomatized. 27 theorems, 484 lines, 9 axioms.
conclusion.implications: The resolution of Weak Goldbach (2013) is a landmark. The binary Goldbach Conjecture (every even n>2 = p+q) remains open. Chen's theorem p+P₂ is the closest result to binary Goldbach.
openQuestions: Prove Binary Goldbach Conjecture: every even n>2 = p+q — major open problem
Formalize Helfgott's complete proof without axioms using Lean's circle method infrastructure
Prove Levy's conjecture: every odd n>5 = p + 2q for primes p, q

crossReferences.description: Both are classic open/resolved problems; Goldbach studies additive prime structure, Ramsey studies combinatorial density
